item.title: UK to pay France £660M in new deal to curb Channel crossings
item.description:
The United Kingdom has agreed to pay France roughly £660 million over three years in a new deal to curb illegal small boat crossings of the English Channel, with Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood set to formally sign the agreement on Thursday, according to the Guardian.

The deal, which will run until March 2029, comes after weeks of fraught negotiations that saw the previous £478 million arrangement expire on March 31 and required a £16.2 million emergency two-month extension to keep patrols running while talks continued.

item.title: US military seizes three Iranian oil tankers in Asian waters
item.description:
The U.S. military intercepted at least three Iranian-flagged oil tankers in Asian waters on Wednesday, redirecting them away from positions near India, Malaysia, and Sri Lanka as Washington extends the enforcement of its naval blockade well beyond the Strait of Hormuz, according to a Reuters exclusive citing shipping and security sources.

The vessels include the supertanker Dorena, fully loaded with roughly 2 million barrels of crude oil and last tracked off the Indian coast, the Deep Sea supertanker, and the smaller tanker Sevin. U.S. Central Command confirmed on Wednesday that the Dorena is under escort by a U.S. Navy destroyer in the Indian Ocean after it attempted to "violate the blockade," and said the total number of vessels directed to turn around or return to port had risen to 29 since the blockade began on April 13.

item.title: Iran denies Trump's claim he stopped execution of eight women
item.description: Iran's judiciary flatly rejected President Donald Trump's assertion that he had intervened to stop the execution of eight women protesters, calling the claim "fake news" and saying the president had been "misled" — setting up a sharp public dispute between Washington and Tehran even as nuclear negotiations continue.

item.title: Google and OpenAI launch rival AI agent platforms on the same day
item.description: The race to define the future of work entered a new phase this week as Google and OpenAI both unveiled AI agent platforms designed to automate office tasks, setting up a direct clash over who will control the next layer of enterprise productivity software.

item.title: Israeli airstrike kills 5 near mosque in northern Gaza
item.description:
An Israeli airstrike struck a group of civilians near the Al-Qassam Mosque in Beit Lahia, northern Gaza, on Wednesday night, killing five Palestinians including three children, according to Gaza's civil defense agency.

"Five Palestinians, including three children, were killed in an Israeli airstrike that targeted a group of civilians near Al-Qassam mosque in Beit Lahia," the agency said in a statement carried by AFP. The bodies were transported to Al-Shifa hospital in Gaza City, which confirmed receiving them. The civil defense did not specify the ages of the children killed. The Israeli military told AFP it was checking the reports.

item.title: Pope Leo visits notorious Equatorial Guinea prison on Africa tour
item.description: Pope Leo XIV visited one of Equatorial Guinea's most notorious correctional facilities on Wednesday, delivering a message of hope to inmates at Bata Prison while drawing attention to the country's long-documented human rights abuses — particularly as the facility has come under renewed scrutiny following U.S. deportations of third-country migrants to the Central African nation.

item.title: Israeli airstrike kills journalist in southern Lebanon
item.description:
Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil was killed on Wednesday in an Israeli airstrike in the southern village of al-Tiri, prompting Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam to accuse Israel of committing war crimes against media workers. Khalil, 43, a reporter for the daily newspaper Al-Akhbar, had been covering renewed hostilities in southern Lebanon when she was struck and buried under rubble for hours before her body could be recovered.

Khalil and freelance photographer Zeinab Faraj were reporting near al-Tiri when an Israeli strike hit a vehicle in front of them. The two journalists ran into a nearby house for cover, which was then also hit by an Israeli strike, according to Lebanon's health ministry and military officials. Faraj sustained a head injury and was evacuated to Tibnin Hospital, where she underwent surgery and is in stable condition. Khalil was trapped beneath the rubble for roughly six hours before rescuers retrieved her body.

item.title: White House says Iran ship seizures don't breach ceasefire
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps seized two commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, hours after President Donald Trump announced an open-ended extension of the U.S.-Iran ceasefire. The White House moved swiftly to minimize the incident, insisting it did not constitute a violation of the truce.

item.title: IDF removes 40 Israeli settlers who crossed into Syria
item.description:
Around 40 Israeli settler activists from the far-right Pioneers of Bashan organization crossed into Syrian territory on Wednesday, barricading themselves on a rooftop on the outskirts of the Druze village of Hader at the foot of Mount Hermon and demanding the Israeli government approve Jewish settlements in Syria.

The Israeli military said the group gathered near the northern border before advancing several hundred meters — roughly half a kilometer — into Syria. IDF troops escorted the activists back to Israeli territory and handed them over to police.

"The IDF strongly condemns this incident and emphasizes its severity, which constitutes a criminal offense that endangers civilians and IDF troops," the military said.

item.title: Asian shares retreat from record highs as oil tops $103 on Iran tensions
item.description: Asian markets pulled back on Thursday after briefly touching record highs, as rising oil prices and uncertainty over the U.S.-Iran conflict prompted investors to lock in profits from a weeks-long technology-driven rally.

item.title: Nuclear leaders convene in Busan, framing reactors as AI-era infrastructure
item.description: As the world prepares to mark the 40th anniversary of the Chernobyl disaster on April 26, the nuclear power industry finds itself in the midst of a striking resurgence. Driven by surging electricity demand from artificial intelligence, climate targets, and fresh government commitments, roughly 75 reactors are now under construction worldwide and about 120 more are planned, according to the World Nuclear Association.

item.title: Tesla raises capex plan to $25 billion for AI push
item.description: Tesla will spend more than $25 billion on capital expenditures this year, roughly tripling last year's outlay, as the electric vehicle maker accelerates its pivot towards artificial intelligence and robotics amid a slowing car business.

item.title: Trump says China helped push Iran toward ceasefire talks
item.description:
As the war between the United States, Israel, and Iran grinds through its second month, China has quietly positioned itself as a pivotal diplomatic player, leveraging its economic ties with Tehran and its desire for global leadership to carve out an outsized role in mediation efforts.

Chinese President Xi Jinping this week called for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz during a phone call with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Monday, reaffirming Beijing's commitment to "all efforts conducive to restoring peace". The intervention followed weeks of intensive behind-the-scenes diplomacy. China's top diplomat Wang Yi made 26 phone calls between the start of the conflict on February 28 and the lead-up to the April 8 ceasefire, according to Al Jazeera.

item.title: U.S.-Iran peace talks stall as Hormuz standoff pushes oil past $100
item.description:
Crude oil prices climbed sharply this week, with Brent crude breaking back above $100 per barrel on Wednesday, as an extended but fragile ceasefire between the United States and Iran failed to ease a mounting maritime standoff in the Strait of Hormuz that continues to choke global energy supplies.

Brent crude rose approximately 3.5 percent on Wednesday to $101.91 per barrel, according to The New York Times, while West Texas Intermediate crude edged up to $92.96. The gains followed a volatile stretch that saw prices jump roughly 5 percent on Tuesday amid uncertainty over the ceasefire's expiration, according to The National.

item.title: Trump says 'no time frame' on Iran war as prices soar
item.description: Nearly two months after the United States and Israel launched airstrikes on Iran on February 28, the economic aftershocks of the conflict continue to ripple across global markets, pushing oil prices to levels not seen in years, raising grocery bills from Washington to Sydney, and sparking a worldwide revival in biofuel investment.

item.title: EU formally approves €90B Ukraine loan, new Russia sanctions
item.description: European Union leaders convened in the Cypriot resort town of Agia Napa on Thursday for a two-day informal summit dominated by the energy crisis triggered by the Strait of Hormuz blockade, the war in Ukraine, and escalating tensions in the Middle East.

item.title: China warns of 'critical juncture' as Iran ceasefire talks falter
item.description: As the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran approaches its third month with a fragile ceasefire hanging in the balance, China has quietly positioned itself as one of the most active diplomatic players working to prevent a return to full-scale hostilities. Beijing's behind-the-scenes efforts — ranging from dozens of high-level phone calls to joint proposals with Pakistan — underscore a broader ambition to reshape its role in Middle Eastern affairs.

item.title: France probes weather sensor tampering tied to Polymarket bets
item.description: French authorities have opened a criminal investigation into the suspected physical manipulation of a weather sensor at Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport after two brief, unexplained temperature spikes this month lined up with winning bets on the cryptocurrency prediction platform Polymarket, netting at least one trader roughly $34,000.

item.title: Interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS traced to cold, ancient corner of the Milky Way
item.description:
A comet that streaked through our solar system from another star likely originated in a frigid, remote region of the galaxy that had yet to form its own planetary system, astronomers announced on Thursday.

Comet 3I/ATLAS, only the third confirmed interstellar visitor and quite possibly the oldest, may be up to 11 billion years old — more than twice the age of our sun, according to the study published in Nature Astronomy.

item.title: 40,000 Samsung workers stage largest protest, threaten strike
item.description: Tens of thousands of Samsung Electronics workers rallied on Thursday at the company's semiconductor complex in Pyeongtaek, South Korea, demanding higher bonuses and threatening an extended strike that could disrupt global AI chip supplies.
